note: Historical per-crate supply-chain AUDIT measurement (paragon axis 1: 'every third-party dependency verified'). cargo-vet remains a SOFT/informational FULL-mode tracker, but the figures below predate AY's migration from sibling paths to an immutable Git source. They must not be presented as current graph coverage until cargo-vet is rerun and first-party AY is classified explicitly.
supply_chain_dir: supply-chain/ (config.toml + audits.toml + imports.lock — audit attestations only, ~70KB; NOT vendored crate source)
scope_note: Historical scope: cargo-vet treated the 27 Clean workspace crates and the former ../ay path stack as first-party/exempt-by-source. AY is now an immutable first-party Git source, so the current classification and counts require a fresh run. The figures below cover only the 2026-06-30 pre-migration graph.
vet_status: STALE: historical Vetting Succeeded result; current AY Git graph not yet measured

coverage_package_versions.comment: cargo-vet's authoritative count is by crate-VERSION over the default-target resolved graph (this is what the gate reports).

coverage_by_crate_name.comment: Deduplicated by crate NAME across versions (a coarser but more intuitive headline).

trusted_imports.comment: Standard, widely-used cargo-vet audit registries pulled into supply-chain/imports.lock. These are the 'verified by reputable third parties' layer. 257 imported audit records + 7 trusted publishers were resolved against our graph.

highest_risk_unaudited.comment: These are exemption-only (NOT covered by any trusted import) and carry the largest native-C/FFI or unsafe surface — the priority targets for the next local audit pass.

native_c_ffi.why: C zstd bindings (build.rs compiles vendored C)
raw FFI to the system libc; huge unsafe surface
FFI to OS entropy syscalls; security-critical
runtime CPU feature detection via asm/FFI

large_unsafe_surface.why: core hashmap with raw-pointer unsafe internals
SIMD byte search with unsafe intrinsics

vendoring_status.summary: cargo-vet records audit ATTESTATIONS only; it does not vendor source. The historical pre-AY-Git graph had an external-source release artifact, but vendoring for the current graph is BLOCKED until third-party-only staging and separate first-party AY/NY subrepo provisioning are implemented.
vendoring_status.internal_repository_policy: AY and every other Andrew Yates internal repository are first-party subrepos and MUST NOT be copied into vendor/ or a vendor release artifact. The recorded artifact predates AY's Git migration; do not refresh it with raw `cargo vendor` until a third-party-only staging flow is in place.
vendoring_status.implemented: Historical pre-AY-Git artifact: a `cargo vendor --versioned-dirs vendor/` tree (385 external crates: 384 crates.io + 1 git carcara, ~522.6MB source -> ~63MB tar.zst) was produced as an OFFLINE-REPRODUCIBLE, TAMPER-EVIDENT release artifact. It remains GITIGNORED and was never committed. The raw command is no longer a valid refresh recipe because it would copy first-party AY.
vendoring_status.tamper_evidence: data/vendor_manifest.json pins every vendored crate by name+version+checksum. crates.io crates use the registry sha256 (asserted equal to Cargo.lock's `checksum =` at generation time); the git crate uses a deterministic sha256 over cargo's per-file checksum map. Regenerate with scripts/gen_vendor_manifest.py and diff to detect source drift.
vendoring_status.offline_wiring: Historical result only: the opt-in .cargo/config.offline.toml resolved the pre-migration graph and compiled clean-kernel. It has no current AY subrepo authority. scripts/build_offline.sh now rejects the stale artifact/current lock pairing before Cargo; no current offline-build claim is made.
vendoring_status.package_verify: scripts/package_vendor.sh {package,verify} tar.zst's the tree with a sha256 sidecar and a re-extract+re-checksum verify step, mirroring crates/clean-mathverse/src/release.rs's package/verify pattern.

enforcement.gate: scripts/local_gate.sh — FULL mode only, SOFT/informational (warn mode, never fail-closed while exemptions remain)
enforcement.ratchet_contract: audited fraction monotonic-up / exemption count monotonic-down. Regenerate after any dep-graph change or new local audit; re-run `cargo vet` + the by-name accounting and update this file. A future hard-gate flip is possible once exemptions reach 0.

follow_ups: Rerun cargo-vet against the current AY Git graph, classify first-party AY explicitly, and replace the historical counts before claiming current coverage.
